20, 1998 {| border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center; border-collapse:collapse;" |- style="background:#efefef;" ! Team 1 ! Result ! Team 2 |- style="" | [[Royal Thai Police FC|Royal Thai Police]] | 0-1 | † [[Osotsapa FC|Osotsapa]] |} † [[Royal Thai Police]] relegated to the [[Thailand Division 1 League]] and [[Osotsapa FC|Osotsapa]] promoted to the [[Thai Premier League]] in next season. ==Season Notes== * [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] were docked three points at the end of season for refusing to play [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] in [[Suphan Buri]] earlier this season. * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|Singha Tero Sasana]] changed the club's name to [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|Tero Sasana]]. * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|Tero Sasana]] represented Thailand in the [[1998–99 Asian Club Championship]] following withdrawals by [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]], [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] and [[Port Authority of Thailand FC|Port Authority of Thailand]], all for economic reasons; [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] qualifier for the [[1998–99 Asian Cup Winners Cup]] after winning [[FA Cup (Thailand)|the Singha FA Cup]]. * Last year's runners-up, [[Stock Exchange of Thailand]], played as Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) owing to a change in sponsorship. ==Queen's Cup== [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] won and retained the [[Queen's Cup (football)|Queen's Cup]] trophy for the 4th year running. This was the 26th edition of the competition. For the first time, no foreign teams took part, owing to the poor economic situation. Thawan Thammaniyai of [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] won the Most Valuable Player award. ==Thailand FA Cup== Sinthana FC won the [[Thailand FA Cup]] for the first time, but it is unclear whom they beat in the final. ==Asian Representation== * [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] represented Thailand in the [[1997–98 Asian Club Championship]], where they would fail in the first round, beaten by Chinese opposition in [[Dalian Wanda]]. * [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] made the second round of the [[1997–98 Asian Cup Winners Cup]], where they were beaten by near neighbours [[PSM Ujungpandang]] of Indonesia after beating [[Melaka Telekom]] of Malaysia in the first round. == Annual awards == === Coach of the Year === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Piyapong Piew-on]] - [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] === Player of the Year === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Seksan Piturat]] - [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] === Top scorer === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Worrawoot Srimaka]] - 17 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] ==Champions== The league champion was [[Air Force United F.C.|Royal Thai Air Force]].
